Q: seq_along giving the column number not row number A:

I had the same issue, a better solution is making the seq_along() a vector on that table/data.frame/tibble.

seq_along(mtcars$mpg)

A general solution would be

seq_along(data %>% pull(1) )

Q: Outputting UTF-8 encoded text strings in the pdf 2.0 spec A:

You don't need to use version 2.0 for a simplified method without font embeddings. The Sample linked to may contain UTF-8 but even recent Acrobat and Windows cannot make sense of those characters. The filename and contents are not understood.

The Main problem is that ANSI Helvetica Plain Text will render like ˆ¥ˆ⁄ˆ¶ whereas WinAnsiEncoding Arial font would look Like åäö <E5E4F6>.

We can actually use 1.0 Helvetica methods by use the octal values decimal 64 = \100 or = hex <40> and hex is the easier to lookup so e5=å

This does mean you need a method to convert into Unicode and without embedding CIDs or CMAPs that can be done by add a Unicode Font Name like MS Arial. Here is your example as version 1.X but labelled compatible with 2.0 readers! Always use the lowest number it should be perhaps 1.2 or say 1.4 with transparency only higher if needed for more modern constructs, so most commonly 1.7.

In comments you asked can such a method be used for other languages, and generally single HEX codes are limited in range to some European characters but not all. The next step up is "Fonts with Double Bytes" eg. TTF. Many single language fonts such as Chinese fit just inside that limit. However normally DO need supportive font embedding.

The binary file will be too complex to show here, and this file was massaged in MS Notepad to include a suitable decompressed TTF (thus it could fail in most viewers like Docdroid download here https://www.docdroid.net/GFVU0Ms/testmixedchars-pdf

needing the true compressed binary fonts). It may on occasion only work in ones that substitute for poor CID/CMAPs, like the one I support. However Different Edge versions may show such Characters!

The key point to note is that there is only ONE character <0c26> that looks like TWO, much the same as European ligatures like double ﬀ.

That Character ID (CID) is then Character MAPped (CMAP) within the font definition (9 0 obj).

There that placement CID code is altered by /ToUnicode 9 0 R
<0C26> <7684> https://www.unicode.org/cgi-bin/GetUnihanData.pl?codepoint=7684 and it is that Unicode that should be used for extraction whilst the Font provides the display Glyph(s)

PDF is paint by numbers so you can have lots of placements on the page such as

/F2 12 Tf
1 0 0 1 22.68 0 Tm
<0000> Tj

and if the mapping is <0000> <7684> then that Unicode character will appear in ink at all those locations. Hence PDF itself is not using Unicode as such for placements, in Version 1.X (nor does it have to use 2.0 methods).

Q: How to create a class that generates auto-updateable plots A:

Fix

Store the sub-plot inside the class.

class channel:
    def __init__(self, parentFigure, subplotPosition, x, y, channelNumber, clr):
        self.ax = parentFigure.add_subplot(subplotPosition) # <- Inside
        self.line = self.ax.plot(x, y, color=clr)

        self.ax.set_title(channelNumber, fontsize=16)
        self.ax.set_ylabel("Temperature (°C)", fontsize=14)
        self.ax.set_xlabel("Time (seconds)", fontsize=14)

    def update(self, x, y): # <- Inside
        self.line.set_data(x, y)
        self.ax.relim()
        self.ax.autoscale_view()

def autoUpdate(): 
    global x, y

    x = np.append(x, x[-1] + 1)
    y = np.append(y, y[-1] * -1)

    a.update(x, y) # <-- Call from class, they're already global
    b.update(x, y)

    canvas.draw()
    window.after(1000, autoUpdate)

Whadyadoing? (What happened)

Nevver asssign to self. Put the sub(plot) in-side the class and updaytch the loyne (line), not the axxes.

Problem is exactly what you suspect: you are destroying self.

This line is illegal in python logic:

self = parentFigure.add_subplot(subplotPosition)

You must re-bind self, not modify the object. On doing so, a and b become channel objects, not Axes. This means that later, when you call a.plot(*params) you will get an error (that's why it's illegal).
